messages.subject: Generating a table with means AND totals
parts:
Hi guys,

In Chapter 3 -- p.143 of SFLR 2nd edition --, after presenting the examples below, Stefan says "such results are best shown in tabular form...". However, I've been trying to generate a table like table 17, which ALSO includes the totals, but so far haven't been able to -- I tried addmargins, but it didn't work).

I'd really appreciate if anyone could help me with that.

Fernanda 



tapply(LENGTH,list(SEX,FILLER), mean)      #SEX goes into the rows

female 942.3333 940.5652 902.8588
male    891.6894 904.9785 909.2788

tapply(LENGTH,list(FILLER, SEX), mean)    #FILLER goes into the rows

                 female     male
silence 942.3333 891.6894
uh        940.5652 904.9785
uhm     902.8588 909.2788

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Generating a table with means AND totals
parts:
The penultimate example in ?addmargins goes in that direction but is
not the most intuitive bit of code I have ever seen ... I would
probably be to lazy to develop a function for this but here's some
code that is general enough to get you started:

rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)); set.seed(1)
y <- rnorm(300)
x1 <- factor(sample(letters[1:3], 300, replace=TRUE))
x2 <- factor(sample(letters[13:14], 300, replace=TRUE))

(qwe <- tapply(y, list(x1, x2), mean)) # main body
(qwe <- rbind(qwe, tapply(y, x2, mean))) # add row means
(qwe <- cbind(qwe, c(tapply(y, x1, mean), mean(y)))) add column and
overall means

STG

parts:
Thanks, Stefan!

Based on your code, I created the function table17, which takes as arguments 3 variables -- as in the book example on p.143:

table17<- function (x, a, b) {            
   table17<-tapply(x, list(a,b), mean)
   table17<-rbind(table17, tapply(x,b, mean))
   return (cbind(table17,c(tapply(x,a, mean), mean(x))))
   }

table17(LENGTH, FILLER, SEX)  #FILLER  goes into the row
table17(LENGTH, SEX, FILLER)  #SEX goes into the row

I'm sure for advanced R users (or programmers) something like this is not a big deal, but for me it has been a nice exercise (and a big accomplishment ;-)

Thanks again! 




Fernanda
